newsitem.title: USA: Mother Teresa in New York to initiate new nuns.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa in New York to initiate new nuns.

text.p: Mother Teresa, looking rested and saying she felt much better, slipped quietly into New York City on Monday where she plans later this week to initiate a group of new nuns into her missionary order.

The Nobel Peace Prize winner, clad in her traditional blue and white sari, gave Virgin Mary medals and a blessing to more than two dozen nuns from the Missionaries of Charity order who met her in an airport lounge shortly after she arrived at John F. Kennedy Airport on a flight from Rome.

Upon her arrival at Rome 10 days ago after a long trip from India, the world-renowned nun, 86, had felt ill and needed oxygen for 20 minutes. At the time, doctors and aides indicated there was no cause for alarm.

Asked how she was feeling in New York, Mother Teresa smiled and said, "Much better." An aide who hovered nearby carried a large case that held a defibrillator in case it was needed. She said her flight from Rome had been "very good."
After 45 minutes greeting and blessing the nuns in the lounge, Mother Teresa was wheeled to a waiting car that took her to a Bronx convent.

On Friday, Mother Teresa participated in a two-hour initiation ceremony in stifling heat in a modern church in Rome in which 16 young women read her their Roman Catholic vows of chastity, poverty and obedience.

Mother Teresa, who was born in Albania and is known as the "saint of the gutter" for her work with the poorest of the poor in Calcutta, India, was taken to a hospital three times last year for emergency care and for heart surgery.
Last Tuesday she held talks in Rome with Pope John Paul II and introduced her successor as head of the Missionaries of Charity order.
Sister Nirmala, a 62-year-old Indian, took over as superior-general of the Calcutta-based order in March when Mother Teresa stepped down after a battle against heart disease.
A sister at the convent in the New York City borough of the Bronx said a schedule of Mother Teresa's appearances would be available later. "Everything depends on her health," she said.
